codex.worst_flaw: The pilot could scale on higher digital completion without establishing that technicians still identify and escalate hazards, because the audit leaves those safety outcomes undefined.

claude.worst_flaw: Crew-level randomisation for a 300-person workforce lacks a sample-size or uncertainty check, and the audit sample of 20 jobs a week cannot reliably catch tick-box completion that was never actually performed. Replayable event and policy versioning is also left unspecified.

holistic.reason: Unusually strong on union trust, anti-gaming audit, safety-hold credit and a randomized comparison, but the no-prize, low-key feedback design may generate modest salience and the lasting effect depends on fixing app friction rather than the campaign itself.

codex.worst_flaw: The scale decision relies on 20 safety audits per week across both groups without defining how much deterioration that sample could reliably detect.

claude.worst_flaw: The design randomises crews but never checks whether a 300-person workforce gives enough crews to detect a 10-point lift, and it leaves out predefined costs, independent shadow validation, versioned policy/event replay and a staffed appeal process with response times.

holistic.reason: Rigorous, union-aware design with a randomized pilot, a diagnosis step, audit sampling and a no-discipline data rule, but the incentive is only a private progress message, so it is easy to overlook and likely to fade once prompts stop.

claude.worst_flaw: The weekly goal is half of expected eligible jobs, capped at three, which signals that skipping digital checks on most jobs is fine for a step that is supposed to happen before every job; the design also never sets a sample size or power for detecting its 10-point scale threshold, and it does not handle spillover between pilot and comparison crews.

codex.worst_flaw: The pilot bundles private feedback, weekly goals and crew reporting, so even a sustained gain would leave the added value of crew reporting unknown.

holistic.reason: Careful, union-aware and safety-conscious with a randomized comparison, but the reward is only private confirmations and a weekly goal, with no tangible incentive or fix for the underlying barriers, so it is likely to be low-salience and fade once the messaging stops.

claude.worst_flaw: The design judges success by a before/after baseline with no concurrent comparison, so it can't separate the programme's effect from the rota and protected time already running in the baseline or from seasonal and workload swings. codex.worst_flaw: The rollout rule relies on a before-and-after comparison that cannot isolate the shared milestone’s effect from private feedback or changes in PR volume and complexity.

holistic.reason: It is carefully designed, private and low-chrome, which suits sceptical engineers, and it fixes coverage first. codex.worst_flaw: The retention rule relies on a 10-point lift from a sequential comparison without accounting for changes in PR case mix, review volume, or sampling uncertainty.

claude.worst_flaw: The evaluation is only a same-team before/after comparison: there is no comparison condition that separates the effect of progress feedback from the review slots and backup routing, and no sample-size or uncertainty plan. holistic.reason: It is careful and sceptic-friendly (private credit, no leaderboards, quality audits, a diagnosis step that fixes blockers first), but the notifications are low-key and the rules are heavy to run for a 25-person team. claude.worst_flaw: The evaluation is only a before/after comparison against a January baseline, with no comparison group and no way to separate plain routing and backup support from the feedback layer. It also names seasonality and workload shifts as confounds without controlling for them, and never says what costs or harms such as author wait time or review depth would block scaling.

codex.worst_flaw: The before-and-after pilot bundles feedback with clearer routing and backup coverage, so it cannot establish whether feedback adds value over those workflow changes alone.

holistic.reason: The proposal is rigorous, privacy-conscious and non-gimmicky (no badges or rankings, a quality gate, a diagnosis step), which suits sceptical engineers. codex.worst_flaw: All three wards add prompts, private goals, and ward reporting at the same time, leaving the expansion decision unable to distinguish the effect of those features from changes over time.

claude.worst_flaw: Learning design relies on a before-and-after comparison across seasons on all three wards, with no concurrent control or plain-support arm, so the plan cannot separate the pilot's added value from secular, seasonal or audit-sampling effects, and the self-reported documentation tick is never shown to improve actual hand hygiene.

holistic.reason: The safety guardrails, privacy limits and pause triggers are unusually thorough, but the design is operationally heavy, asks busy nurses to add kiosk logging with only a private two-tick goal as motivation, and it deliberately removes the prompts after April, so little reason remains for the habit to persist.

codex.worst_flaw: All three wards add and remove milestones on the same schedule, so the pilot cannot distinguish their effect from growing familiarity with the kiosk or changes in the mix of observed cases.

claude.worst_flaw: The adoption decision relies on a before/after comparison within each ward, with no concurrent comparison ward or plain-support arm. That makes it hard to separate the milestone mechanic's effect from secular trends and from observers changing behaviour.

holistic.reason: The proposal is safety-conscious, privacy-protective and measures independently through audits, so I would approve it, but the rewards are only private confirmations and progress messages, which are weak motivators for busy nurses, and it removes the prompts and goals two months before the follow-up, so I expect the logging habit to fade.

claude.worst_flaw: Matching kiosk entries one-to-one to observed actions by temporary nurse code, time and indication is a fragile core measurement with no shadow validation of match accuracy or inter-observer reliability, and with three wards and a single comparison ward, the 10-point scale rule cannot separate the programme's effect from ward differences.

codex.worst_flaw: With one comparison ward and no preset minimum audit sample or case-mix adjustment, the scale-up rule can mistake shifts in which hand-hygiene opportunities are observed for a programme effect.

holistic.reason: The measurement design is rigorous, privacy-safe, and has safety pauses, but it's complex to operate and the nurse-facing motivation is weak (practice entries, a single thank-you note, no real reward), so uptake and post-pilot persistence look modest.

codex.worst_flaw: The pilot bundles prompts, goals, and shared progress without specifying a plain-feedback comparison arm, so the results cannot show which additions are worth keeping.

claude.worst_flaw: With only 60 agents, a comparison of a few teams has no stated sample size or uncertainty plan, so the +10-point scale rule could be driven by noise or differences in team case mix; it also lacks replayable event and policy versioning and a staffed, independent appeal path beyond the existing support channel.

holistic.reason: Rigorous measurement, fairness rules and CSAT guardrails make it safe to approve, but with no cash value and mostly private progress messages the incentive is weak, so agents may not notice or care and the habit likely fades once prompts are removed.

codex.worst_flaw: The uniform 50% weekly goal has no baseline or feasibility justification for agents whose eligible tickets require substantial authoring and editorial review.

claude.worst_flaw: The weekly goal is set at half of eligible tickets with no link to the 12% baseline or to agent feasibility, and with about 60 agents the randomised team comparison has too few clusters to reliably detect the 15-point threshold. The design does not acknowledge this power limit.

holistic.reason: The measurement, QA and privacy safeguards are careful, and keeping the programme away from CSAT pay is sound. codex.worst_flaw: The pilot gives only the programme teams private progress feedback and recognition, so it cannot tell whether recognition adds value over plain feedback.

claude.worst_flaw: The test randomises a handful of existing teams in a 60-person org with fixed 10/5-point thresholds and a 2-point CSAT limit, but never deals with how few clusters there are, statistical uncertainty or low CSAT response counts, so the scale/stop decision may rest on noise.

holistic.reason: The measurement, audit and randomised-pilot design is rigorous, but the only incentive is a weekly counter and one private thank-you, with no reward or friction removal.
